applies_why: The judge text resolves a Luke 2:48-49 collision by saying Mary's phrase is immediately qualified by the child's reference, which is the kind of verse-by-verse treatment K-C governs against a chain-press.
quote: Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" — I weighed whether it forbids using Luke 2:49 to qualify Luke 2:48 when the press is chain-based, or only forbids deciding by whether one verse states the contrary; I read it as requiring chain-against-chain footing here.
why: The judge resolves the collision by an immediate verse-level qualification of Mary's phrase rather than weighing the pressing chain against the link by footing as K-C requires.
